findings.title: pruneTraces() now carries four near-identical batch-delete loops instead of one shared helper
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/lib/reconciler.mjs:150-216. The #1046 diff adds two more copies (prunedInvitePreviewAttempts at lines 185-199, prunedConfirmationAttempts at lines 201-215) of the exact same shape already used for `pruned` (line 137ish) and `prunedWorkTraces` (lines 150-168): a `for` loop up to maxBatches, a try/catch swallowing only `42883` (undefined_function), accumulate `n`, break when `n < batch`. The only per-copy variance is the SQL text and the accumulator/param names.
findings.required_fix: Judgement call, not a hard violation — the diff follows an existing (already-smelly) local convention rather than introducing a new one. Fowler's fix applies: extract one `pruneBatched(client, {sql, unit, amount, batch, maxBatches})` helper and call it four times; would remove roughly 35 duplicated lines. A documented repo standard does not forbid this shape and the ticket's own report cites the precedent explicitly as deliberate ('the same batched-loop way prune_trace_spans / prune_work_execution_traces are already called'), so this is reported as a smell to weigh, not a rule violation.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a correctness risk today (all four loops are independently well-tested and green), but a fifth evidence table needing the same retention treatt would be the third copy-paste, compounding the drift risk Duplicated Code names: a bug fixed in one copy (as very nearly happened here — see the 0348 floor-check vacuity-control bug) has three more places it could still be lurking.
